Hazardous Waste Handler – Floater

Location: San Diego, CA

Pay: $25–$30 per hour

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 6:00 AM–4:00 PM

CDL: Not required

Mileage: Reimbursed

Position Overview

We are seeking a dependable, positive, self-motivated Hazardous Waste Handler to service multiple client locations throughout San Diego County, including La Jolla, Carlsbad, Escondido, Oceanside, and Rancho Bernardo.

This is a hands-on, general labor and environmental services position. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who takes initiative, works independently, has a strong work ethic, and enjoys interacting with customers.

This is NOT a laboratory or chemist position. The role focuses on general labor, hazardous waste management, regulatory compliance, customer service, and facility inspections.

Key Responsibilities

Perform hands-on general labor and hazardous waste handling.
Manage, organize, label, segregate, and maintain hazardous waste in accordance with applicable regulations.
Monitor waste accumulation areas and ensure compliance with RCRA and other applicable environmental requirements.
Conduct routine facility inspections and identify potential compliance issues.
Maintain accurate inspection records, waste logs, and required documentation.
Service client locations and maintain positive customer relationships.
Communicate professionally with customers regarding waste management needs and compliance concerns.
Identify issues, take initiative, and help resolve problems.
Maintain clean, organized, and compliant waste storage areas.
Travel between multiple customer sites throughout the assigned service territory.

Ideal Candidate

Positive attitude and professional demeanor.
Self-starter with strong self-motivation.
Dependable, punctual, and organized.
Comfortable performing physical, hands-on general labor.
Able to work independently and manage multiple client locations.
Strong customer service and communication skills.
Detail-oriented with the ability to recognize compliance issues.
Takes ownership of responsibilities and follows through on tasks.
Willingness to learn environmental regulations and waste management procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

40-Hour HAZWOPER certification.
RCRA training or experience.
Previous hazardous waste handling experience.
Environmental services or industrial general labor experience.
Experience conducting inspections and maintaining compliance documentation.

Clean Harbors is looking for Chemical Handlers to join our safety conscious team!  

Do you enjoy...    

Staying active and on your feet?
Learning and applying knowledge about science and chemistry? 
Working directly with customers?

Why work for Clean Harbors?

Health and Safety is our #1 priority, and we live it 3-6-5!  
Competitive wages and generous paid time off

Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career!

Responsibilities

Wondering what to expect in starting a career at Clean Harbors?

InSite Technicians perform a wide range of tasks, including:

Packaging and labeling waste products to maximize efficiency and maintain compliance;

Operating forklifts;

This position is an entry level role, but many of our leaders started in this job! With safety as our top priority, you'll get the training and support to not only succeed at your job but advance your career.

added.title: Environmental Scientist
added.description:
Job Title: Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist)

Job Description

This Environmental Scientist (Staff Scientist) role focuses on designing, supervising, and executing complex laboratory and field studies that assess the behavior and persistence of chemicals in the environment. The position plays a key role in delivering high-quality, regulatory-compliant environmental fate and ecotoxicology data to a global clientele across agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, and animal health products. You will act as a technical expert, provide guidance to colleagues and clients, and contribute to the development of procedures, methods, and reports that support global regulatory submissions.

Responsibilities

Design and supervise simple and complex experiments and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including but not limited to DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD guidelines.
Develop procedures and methods to solve technical problems and improve laboratory practices and workflows.
Serve as a technical expert for staff and external customers, providing scientific guidance and support on environmental fate and related studies.
Perform advanced troubleshooting of instrumentation and equipment to ensure accurate and reliable data generation.
Conduct studies to determine the persistence, distribution, and behavior of chemicals in various environmental matrices such as soil, water, and other media.
Perform complex data evaluations, interpret results, and ensure scientific integrity and accuracy in all analyses.
Review the work and data generated by other staff members to ensure compliance with quality standards and regulatory requirements.
Write complex technical reports, including study reports and standard operating procedures, that clearly document methods, results, and conclusions.
Serve as a primary business contact for clients on assigned projects, providing updates, clarifying technical issues, and ensuring customer satisfaction.
Work concurrently on multiple projects, effectively prioritizing tasks and managing timelines to meet project and regulatory deadlines.
Monitor and direct activities of other staff within your area of expertise, offering technical leadership and mentoring.
Potentially serve as Study Director on one or more projects, overseeing Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance and ensuring that all work on assigned projects meets regulatory and internal quality standards.
Confer with scientists and colleagues to plan research, discuss findings, and prepare technical papers and reports.
Train staff on laboratory techniques, methods, and procedures necessary to complete environmental fate and related laboratory assignments.
Maintain accurate records, follow established protocols and company policies, and support continuous improvement of laboratory operations.

Essential Skills

Demonstrated experience working in a GLP-compliant laboratory environment, including adherence to regulatory standards such as DEA, EPA, FDA, FIFRA, and OECD.
Strong Expereince in environmental science, environmental fate studies, or closely related disciplines.
Proficiency in chemistry and analytical chemistry, including chemical testing and wet chemistry techniques.
Experience in environmental fate studies that evaluate the persistence and behavior of chemicals in environmental matrices.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance and environmental field practices, including soil sampling and remediation concepts.
Familiarity with laboratory operations, quality control procedures, and environmental engineering or environmental remediation principles.
Ability to perform advanced troubleshooting of scientific instrumentation and laboratory equipment.
Strong computer skills and the ability to use scientific software and data analysis tools effectively.
Excellent scientific and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize tasks.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to write complex technical reports and standard operating procedures.
High attention to detail and a commitment to data integrity and quality.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, demonstrating self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude.
Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, and maintain accurate and complete records.
Bachelors degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or another directly related discipline.
Minimum of five years of experience in an environmental fate laboratory with direct involvement in GLP studies.
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Masters degree in a relevant field such as chemistry, biochemistry, biology, environmental science, or related discipline.
At least three years of directly relevant experience in an environmental fate laboratory when combined with a Masters degree, as a substitute for the bachelors degree plus five years of experience.
Experience in microbiology, biology, toxicology, or related life science disciplines.
Expereince in environmental engineering, environmental remediation, or related environmental fields.
Experience with analytical chemistry and wet chemistry methods applied to environmental and chemical testing.
Familiarity with laboratory-based quality control systems and procedures.
Experience as a Study Director or in project management within a GLP laboratory environment.
Experience working with agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, or animal health products in a testing or research setting.
Ability to collaborate with a global client base and provide clear technical explanations to non-specialist stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates in both laboratory and field environments, providing exposure to a wide range of environmental and analytical testing activities. You will work in a highly specialized laboratory recognized for high-tier ecotoxicology and environmental fate studies that support global regulatory requirements for agrochemicals, industrial chemicals, pharmaceuticals, biocides, and animal health products. The site is known for its long-tenured staff, with many team members having 1020 years of experience, creating a stable, collaborative, and knowledge-rich environment. The organization is part of a large international life sciences network with hundreds of laboratories worldwide, offering access to advanced technologies, diverse scientific expertise, and opportunities to contribute to complex, high-impact projects across food, environmental, pharmaceutical, genomics, forensics, and advanced material sciences testing. The standard schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with overtime as needed to meet project and regulatory deadlines. Work involves typical laboratory attire and adherence to safety protocols, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment in both lab and field settings.

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Easton, MD.

Pay And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $28.84 - $43.26/hr.

Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.

Description

The Assistant Environmental Scientist will assist in and conduct environmental assessments, supporting environmental compliance efforts, preparing permitting applications and analyzing environmental data for various types of projects, including power generation and electrical transmission construction activities, oil & gas activities, renewable projects, industrial sites and water treatment facilities.

Assist in conducting field surveys, environmental compliance audits and assessments and collecting project-related data.

Assist with performing environmental site investigations, support erosion control efforts and subsurface soil sampling.
Assist in conducting environmental compliance audits.
Assist in preparing a wide variety of permitting applications such as storm water, land use and local permits.
Assist with observing and documenting environmental compliance on construction projects and industrial sites.
Ensure compliance with company and site safety policies.
All other duties as assigned.

Ability to clearly communicate both verbal and written technical information.

Lead and inspire Council’s Environment Team in delivering services that protect and enhance community wellbeing and our natural environment.

the assessment of development referrals for environmental aspects such as land contamination, acoustics, air quality, and wastewater management;
the implementation of Councils onsite wastewater management program;

Developing environmental health policies and procedures.

’.

We’ve got an opportunity, you’ve got talent… Let’s talk.

Summary

Organizational Location: This position is with the Department of Homeland Security, within U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM), Integrated Services (IS) Division, Energy and Environmental Program Management Office (EE PMO). There is (1) vacancy that may be filled in one of the following locations: Indianapolis, IN Washington, DC Aliso Viejo, CA

Duties

This position is located in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Enterprise Services (ES), Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM), Integrated Services Division (IS), Energy and Environmental Program Management Office (EE PMO). The Integrated Services Division's Energy and Environmental Program Management Office (EE PMO) includes the Execution Team, Environmental Section, and Energy Section. The EE PMO interprets environmental, energy, and resilience requirements; coordinates with stakeholders to ensure planning and regulatory compliance throughout the facility and non-facility lifecycle; leads coordination on related priorities with DHS and other federal, state, local, and tribal agencies; and develops agency-wide directives, policies, and guidance. Typical duties may include: Serving as the agency representative for energy and environmental management programs. Developing and administering policies supporting compliance with environmental and energy laws, regulations, executive requirements, and agency directives. Coordinating and negotiating with federal, state, and local officials on environmental, energy, and legislative matters affecting program operations. Directing subordinate supervisors and staff performing technical, professional, and administrative work. Managing workforce planning, recruitment, performance appraisals, employee development, awards, and related supervisory functions. This position starts at a salary of $147,945.00 (GS-15, Step 1) to $192,331.00 (GS-15, Step 10). Salary: Salary listed reflects the rest of U.S. scale and, if applicable, will be adjusted to meet the locality pay or cost of living expenses of the duty location upon selection. Requiremennts

Your conduct will be subject to the ethics rules applicable to all Executive Branch employees, and to CBP employees specifically, as well as the criminal conflict of interest statutes. Once you enter on duty, these rules include obtaining approval for outside employment or business activity, to ensure such employment or business activity is not prohibited and does not interfere or conflict with performance of your official duties. Please review further details via the following link. DHS uses E-Verify, an internet-based system, to confirm the eligibility of all newly hired employees to work in the United States. Learn more about E-Verify including your rights and responsibilities. Financial Disclosure is required. Bargaining Unit: This position is not covered under the bargaining unit. This position requires the employee to travel away from the normal duty station up to 25% of the time. This position is considered key emergency essential.

Qualifications

Experience: You qualify for the GS-15 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Managing energy, environmental, sustainability, resilience, or compliance programs, including program operations, support services, priorities, and strategic initiatives. Coordinating with senior leaders, field offices, program staff, or external partners to implement environmental or energy requirements and resolve program issues. Developing work plans, schedules, priorities, procedures, or action plans to meet short- and long-term program goals. Reviewing program data, reports, projects, or performance results to identify compliance concerns, resource issues, process gaps, or needed corrective actions. Leading supervisors, team leads, or program staff by assigning work, tracking progress, resolving barriers, and improving program performance. NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible. Please see the "Required Documents" section below for additional resume requirements. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You must: Meet all qualification requirements, including education if applicable to this position, subject to verification at any stage of the application process; and Meet all applicable Time in Grade requirements (current federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade or equivalent grade band in the federal service) by 11/09/2026. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. This position is located in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Enterprise Services (ES), Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM), Integrated Services Division (IS), Energy and Environmental Program Management Office (EE PMO). The Integrated Services Division's Energy and Environmental Program Management Office (EE PMO) includes the Execution Team, Environmental Section, and Energy Section. The EE PMO interprets environmental, energy, and resilience requirements; coordinates with stakeholders to ensure planning and regulatory compliance throughout the facility and non-facility lifecycle; leads coordination on related priorities with DHS and other federal, state, local, and tribal agencies; and develops agency-wide directives, policies, and guidance. Typical duties may include: Serving as the agency representative for energy and environmental management programs. Developing and administering policies supporting compliance with environmental and energy laws, regulations, executive requirements, and agency directives. Coordinating and negotiating with federal, state, and local officials on environmental, energy, and legislative matters affecting program operations. Directing subordinate supervisors and staff performing technical, professional, and administrative work. Managing workforce planning, recruitment, performance appraisals, employee development, awards, and related supervisory functions. This position starts at a salary of $147,945.00 (GS-15, Step 1) to $192,331.00 (GS-15, Step 10). added.title: Water Resources Project Manager
added.description:
What We're Looking For

Are you looking for a new, exciting opportunity? We are seeking a highly creative and motivated engineering project manager with experience in water resources to lead project design. While the primary focus will be on local and statewide projects with municipal clients and the DOT, the candidate will have the opportunity to support other disciplines and projects through our firmwide practice. Join our more than 110 years of experience and be part of why HNTB consistently ranks as a top design firm nationwide by Engineering News-Record (ENR).

At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners.

This opportunity entails being responsible for managing assigned project(s) throughout their full lifecycle including developing the scope and technical sections of proposal and procurement documents to participating in contract negotiations and overseeing the delivery of the project plan to successfully accomplish HNTB’s 4 for 4 performance: delivery of quality work, on time, on budget and to the client’s satisfaction on every project. This position proactively manages the budget, schedule, technical requirements, contractual obligations, and client communications in support of the project’s objectives. Provides high level technical tasks while managing and reviewing design related specifications, calculations, reports and plans. Coordinates with internal and external partners including cross-discipline and functional teams to address and problem solve design related issues or concerns. The Project Manager I – Engineering typically manages project team(s) for one or more strategic (<$1M) projects or may lead and/or work as a discipline lead on a mini-mega ($1M to <$5M) project management team.

What You'll Do

Responsible for development of the project scope and fee quotation and assists in the preparation of technical proposals and contracts in accordance with HNTB's Sophisticated Contracting Approach (SCA).
Serves as the primary client liaison and manages the project team to deliver the scope, schedule, and budgets to completion and to the client’s satisfaction. Assists with client project scoping and contract negotiations.
Performs technical discipline tasks including analysis, reports, design, specification, and production for assigned projects.
Implements the firm’s project delivery plan using HNTB's Sophisticated Delivery Approach (SDA) on each project. Leads the development and the execution of the project management plan. Supervises and mentors team to overall project objectives.
Performs coordination with managers on project staffing, including, but not limited to; recruitment, development, retention, and succession of project staff; development of plan for project staff reporting; and support for performance and compensation reviews.
Partners with Client Service Leaders and pursuit champions to assist with business development, building client relationships, and pursuit efforts for strategic and mini-mega projects in accordance with HNTB's Sophisticated Sales Approach (SSA). Works with the project team and marketing resources to prepare appropriate proposal and presentation materials. Leads proposal development and interview presentations for strategic and mini-mega projects to the client as well as general presentations within the industry and community.
May be responsible for the recruitment, hiring, development, and retention of staff, including development of plan for staff reporting, performance and compensation reviews, and succession.
Performs other duties as assigned.

What You'll Need

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering and 8 years of relevant experience
2 years task management or Deputy PM experience

What You'll Bring

Winning, contracting, and successfully delivering 4for4 (on-time, on-budget, quality, client satisfaction) on smaller projects. Identifying and escalating risk and change management issues, with oversight from more experienced staff.
Leading a team for a smaller project or task order with no or few subconsultants.
Using system tools to manage, monitor, and deliver smaller projects or task orders.
Leveraging the Office Management Team to assist in implementing HNTB Sophisticated processes as applicable to the project.
Interfacing with your client-level peer on a smaller project or task order.
Providing technical guidance to team and task leads as well as performing portions of the technical work. **

What We Prefer

Master’s degree in Engineering
10 years relevant experience
Professional Engineer (PE) certification
American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) certification
Project Management Professional (PMP)
Local municipal and/or DOT experience and relationships
Active engagement in local professional and/or civic organizations
Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Additional Information

Click here to learn more about Equal Opportunity Employer/Disability/Veteran

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
